hunks.baseline: The haze of magical power faintly wrapping around the surroundings. The monsters’ corpses piled up like mountains, and the surviving monsters’ roars.
hunks.sol: The faint haze of magical power around me, the mountains of monster corpses, the roars of the monsters that had survived—all of it vanished.

hunks.baseline: Everything around me vanished.
There was only one thing.
Far away, a man with pitch-black hair hanging down like a cloak, and the pure-white skeleton in his hand, burned into my retinas.
hunks.sol: Only one sight remained: far away, a man with pitch-black hair hanging down like a cloak held a pure-white skeleton in his hand. The two of them were burned into my retinas as though they were the only things left in the world.

hunks.baseline: As if they were the only things in the world.
“What are you holding in your hand?”
hunks.sol: “What are you holding?”

hunks.baseline: My restrained voice crossed the hundred or so meters between us. At the other end stood a man gazing at me in silence.
hunks.sol: My restrained voice crossed the hundred or so meters between us. At the other end stood a man gazing silently at me.

hunks.baseline: A beauty that seemed to belong to another world, and an evil so pure it was all the more horrifying, spilled from his lips.
hunks.sol: His voice was beautiful enough to seem otherworldly, and carried an evil so pure it was all the more horrifying.

hunks.baseline: “A clue that may satisfy my long-held desire, and a very valuable trophy.”
hunks.sol: “A clue to satisfying a desire I’ve held for a very long time. And a valuable trophy.”

hunks.baseline: Morgoth added, one corner of his mouth curling upward.
hunks.sol: One corner of Morgoth’s mouth curled upward.

hunks.baseline: “The friendship between a human and a monster. It was a moving story. Judging by the fact that you came here alone, it seems it was all true.”
hunks.sol: “A friendship between a human and a monster. A moving story. Judging by the fact that you’ve come here alone, it seems it was all true.”

hunks.baseline: I didn’t know.
I didn’t know exactly what had happened here.
hunks.sol: I didn’t know exactly what had happened here, or what had been said.

hunks.baseline: Or what had been said.
The Skeleton King had done everything he could, and he had done it for me—for all of us.
hunks.sol: The Skeleton King had done everything he could, and he’d done it for me—for all of us.

hunks.baseline: That was why I couldn’t ask the most important question. His obsidian eyes watched me closely, taking in every part of me.
hunks.sol: That was why I couldn’t bring myself to ask the question that mattered most. Morgoth’s obsidian eyes took in every bit of my hesitation.

hunks.baseline: As if he’d read my mind, he asked. I gave him a brief answer.
hunks.sol: As if he’d read my mind. I answered briefly.

hunks.baseline: “There’s a crazy Dragon standing in front of me, and he’s holding someone I know very well. I want that guy to still be alive.”
hunks.sol: “There’s a crazy Dragon standing in front of me, and he’s holding someone I know very well. I want him to still be alive.”

hunks.baseline: Maybe it was my unhesitating answer. After a brief silence, Morgoth gave a quiet laugh.
hunks.sol: Maybe it was how readily I’d answered. After a brief silence, Morgoth gave a quiet laugh.

hunks.baseline: “So, your answer?”
hunks.sol: “So? Your answer?”

hunks.baseline: “Didn’t I already tell you? A valuable trophy. He was so violent in his rampage that he’s a little damaged, but I have no desire to see him shattered to pieces.”
hunks.sol: “Didn’t I already tell you? He’s a valuable trophy. He fought so violently that he’s a little damaged, but I have no desire to see him shattered to pieces.”

hunks.baseline: The meaning behind those words was clear.
hunks.sol: The meaning was clear.

hunks.baseline: Right. He was still alive.
hunks.sol: He was still alive.

hunks.baseline: That bastard, the Skeleton King.
hunks.sol: That bastard. The Skeleton King.

hunks.baseline: The answer I’d been desperately waiting for ever since setting foot in this godforsaken ruin.
hunks.sol: It was the answer I’d been desperately waiting for since the moment I set foot in this godforsaken ruin. Only then did I let out the breath I’d been holding.

hunks.baseline: Only then did I let out the breath I’d been holding. I put my whole heart into my words.
“Don’t mention it. I couldn’t pass up such a precious opportunity after all this time.”
hunks.sol: “Don’t mention it. I couldn’t let such a precious opportunity pass me by.”

hunks.baseline: “You don’t have a hobby of taking hostages, do you?”
hunks.sol: “You don’t make a habit of taking hostages, do you?”

hunks.baseline: “Hostage-taking? My intellect and stature are far too great for such a cheap amusement.”
hunks.sol: “Hostage-taking? My intellect and stature are far too great for such cheap amusement.”

hunks.baseline: “Perhaps. Or perhaps it’s the worst news you could have heard. I make a clear distinction between trophies and everything else.”
hunks.sol: “Perhaps. Or perhaps it’s the worst news you could have heard. I draw a clear distinction between trophies and everything else.”

hunks.baseline: “If something is too dangerous to possess, then it must be destroyed. That way, there won’t be any trouble later.”
hunks.sol: “If something is too dangerous to possess, it must be destroyed. That way, there’s no trouble later.”

hunks.baseline: Magical power churned around us.
hunks.sol: Magical power churned around us. A wave of power, unbelievably pure and vast.

hunks.baseline: An unbelievably pure, colossal wave of power.
And a murderous intent so vivid it felt within reach.
hunks.sol: And murderous intent so vivid I could almost touch it.

hunks.baseline: “Were you planning this from the start?”
hunks.sol: “Was this your plan from the start?”

hunks.baseline: “No. But the moment we first met, I realized I might make the same mistake Asmodeus once did. And, more than anything…”
hunks.sol: “No. But the moment I first saw you, I realized I might make the same mistake Asmodeus once did. And more than anything…”

hunks.baseline: His unpleasant gaze, a mixture of interest and regret, pierced through me as if it could see right through my body.
hunks.sol: His gaze swept over me, unpleasant in its mixture of interest and regret, as though it could see through my entire body.

hunks.baseline: His hair, long enough to reach the ground, floated into the air.
hunks.sol: His hair, long enough to reach the ground, rose into the air like the wings of a being from myth.

hunks.baseline: Like the wings of a being from myth.
hunks.sol: Not an angel’s wings. A demon’s.

hunks.baseline: Except they belonged to a demon, not an angel.
Silence passed for an instant. I opened my mouth.
hunks.sol: For an instant, silence hung between us. Then I spoke.

hunks.baseline: A Hunter—the sword and shield that protects humanity, and a hunter.
hunks.sol: A Hunter. A sword and shield for humanity, and a hunter.

hunks.baseline: But that wasn’t the only reason I intended to face him head-on.
hunks.sol: But that wasn’t the only reason I’d come to face him head-on.

hunks.baseline: If Morgoth had really been someone I could trust, I would have gladly done whatever he wanted.

hunks.baseline: I would have prostrated myself before him. If he’d told me to cut off my own arms and legs, I would have done it.
hunks.sol: If Morgoth had truly been someone I could trust, I would have gladly done whatever he wanted. I would have bowed at his feet. If he’d told me to cut off my own arms and legs, I would have done it.

hunks.baseline: If the deaths of Cheon Taemin and me could bring peace to billions of people, I would have given them up without a second thought.
hunks.sol: If Cheon Taemin and I could bring peace to billions by dying, I would have given it up without a second thought.

hunks.baseline: But just as Morgoth had, I understood with absolute clarity the moment I faced him.
hunks.sol: But just as Morgoth had understood something when he first saw me, I’d understood something about him.

hunks.baseline: Those eyes, so clear they seemed pure, were no different from those of a child watching an ant crawl across the asphalt on a midsummer afternoon.
hunks.sol: They were so clear they seemed pure—and no different from a child’s eyes as he watched an ant crawl across the asphalt on a midsummer afternoon.

hunks.baseline: And one more thing.
hunks.sol: And there was one more thing.

hunks.baseline: With a voice boiling over, strange enough to sound like someone else’s, I took a step.
hunks.sol: My voice boiled over, so strange it sounded like someone else’s. I took a step.

hunks.baseline: As my foot came down with more force than ever before, memories as vivid as yesterday sank deeper than its imprint.
hunks.sol: As I put my foot down harder than ever before, memories as vivid as yesterday sank in deeper than the footprint it left.

hunks.baseline:
> “Human, instead of that, how about making a deal with me?”
>
> “A deal?”
hunks.sol:
> “Human, why don’t you make a deal with me instead?”
>
> “A deal?”

hunks.baseline: A-rank Gate, the Black Forest of the Black Wizard.
hunks.sol: An A-rank Gate. The Black Forest of the Black Wizard.

hunks.baseline: I couldn’t say exactly when it happened.
When I began to see him as more than just a monster.
hunks.sol: I couldn’t say exactly when it had happened—when I’d begun to see him as more than just a monster.

hunks.baseline: That day, I’d told him as he brooded that I didn’t really know, but he’d probably been a pretty decent guy.
hunks.sol: That day, I’d told him I didn’t really know, but he’d probably been a pretty decent guy. I’d let the words slip almost to myself, embarrassed for no good reason.

hunks.baseline: And he hadn’t forgotten the words I’d let slip as if talking to myself, embarrassed for no good reason.
hunks.sol: He hadn’t forgotten them.

hunks.baseline: Even now, the memory stood clear before my eyes.
hunks.sol: Even now, I could see it all clearly.

hunks.baseline: The Skeleton King forcing his way out of my Inventory by his own power and shielding me with his entire body.
hunks.sol: The sight of him forcing his way out of my Inventory by his own power and shielding me with his entire body.

hunks.baseline: The voice I’d thought I would never hear again.
hunks.sol: That voice I’d thought I would never hear again.

hunks.baseline: Only after hearing my answer did his dim ghostly eyes curve like a crescent moon.
hunks.sol: Only after hearing my answer did the dim lights in his eyes curve like a crescent moon.

hunks.baseline: > “You asked why.”
hunks.sol: > “You asked me why.”

hunks.baseline: Then, on human land, a new being who’d sacrificed himself to protect humans rose once more with a shining crown.
hunks.sol: Then, on human soil, a new being who’d sacrificed himself to protect a human rose again with a shining crown.

hunks.baseline: Returning the words I’d once said to him—the words someone would never forget.
hunks.sol: He gave back the words I’d once said to him—words he would never forget.

hunks.baseline: I was burning up.
The eyes fixed solely on Morgoth.
hunks.sol: Hot.

hunks.baseline: The two dantians that, like a volcano erupting after a long wait, poured forth Scorching Yang Qi without pause.
hunks.sol: My eyes, fixed solely on Morgoth. My two dantians, pouring out Scorching Yang Qi without pause like a volcano erupting after a long wait.

hunks.baseline: And the step I took, carrying every memory that had just passed through me.
hunks.sol: Even the step I took, carrying every memory that had just passed through me.

hunks.baseline: A deep rumble spread.
The devastated ground crumbled again.
hunks.sol: A deep rumble spread. The devastated ground crumbled again.

hunks.baseline: No—“vaporized” might have been more accurate.
hunks.sol: No—*vaporized* might have been more accurate.

hunks.baseline: The heat Morgoth felt was that horrifyingly intense, and the speed surpassed even sound.
hunks.sol: The heat Morgoth felt was that intense, and the speed surpassed even sound.

hunks.baseline: The Black Dragon’s obsidian eyes flashed as they read and saw through everything.

preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: The streak of fire rushing up to his face—and something that suddenly emerged from within its immense heat.
hunks.sol: The Black Dragon’s obsidian eyes flashed as he read it all: the streak of fire rushing up to his face, and something suddenly emerging from its immense heat.

hunks.baseline: Morgoth’s eyes flew wide. In them, a silver spearhead slashed down at an angle.
hunks.sol: Morgoth’s eyes flew wide. A silver spearhead slashed down at an angle, reflected in them.

hunks.baseline: He hadn’t sensed the power of any magic.
hunks.sol: He hadn’t sensed any magic.

hunks.baseline: But before he could find an answer, the flames riding the spearhead thrust into his chest.
hunks.sol: Before he could find an answer, the flames carried on the spearhead drove into his chest.

hunks.baseline: *Tap. Slice!*
hunks.sol: *Flash—slice!*

hunks.baseline: In a moment split into smaller moments, Morgoth crossed the distance in an instant. He silently raised a hand to touch the area around his chest.
hunks.sol: In an instant split into countless smaller moments, Morgoth crossed the distance in a single leap. Silently, he raised a hand to his chest.

hunks.baseline: More precisely, the patch of skin that had been scorched black by the slightest graze.
hunks.sol: More precisely, to the patch of skin that had been scorched black by the slightest graze.

hunks.baseline: The third time in thousands of years that he’d felt pain.
hunks.sol: It was only the third time in thousands of years that he’d felt pain.

hunks.baseline: But unlike the undead monster that had inflicted the second pain on him, the human approaching from afar with his spearhead lowered still held immense power.
hunks.sol: But unlike the undead monster who’d caused him pain the second time, the human approaching from afar with his spear lowered still held immense power.

hunks.baseline: Enough to make Morgoth ask with genuine curiosity:
hunks.sol: Enough to make Morgoth ask with genuine curiosity, “Are you, by any chance, one of my kind?”

hunks.baseline: “Are you, by any chance, one of my kind?”
Slowly but carefully closing the distance, Jin Taekyung answered calmly.
hunks.sol: Jin Taekyung closed the distance slowly, cautiously.

hunks.baseline: “Your vulgar speech makes it certain you’re not one of my kind…but how can a human grow so strong so quickly?”
hunks.sol: “Your vulgar speech makes it clear you’re not one of my kind…but how can a human grow so strong so quickly?”

hunks.baseline: How could it be so fascinating?
hunks.sol: How could that not fascinate him?

hunks.baseline: But Morgoth had to force down the curiosity that rose unexpectedly from deep within him.
hunks.sol: But Morgoth forced down the curiosity rising from deep within him. The human before him was too dangerous to let a moment’s curiosity distract him.

hunks.baseline: The human before him was dangerous enough that he couldn’t afford to be swept away by a moment’s curiosity.
“I’m afraid I’ll never get to hear that interesting story of yours.”
hunks.sol: “A pity. I’ll never get to hear that interesting story of yours.”

hunks.baseline: With a low mutter, Morgoth clenched both hands like claws and grasped at empty air.
hunks.sol: Muttering under his breath, Morgoth curled both hands like claws and seized the empty air.

hunks.baseline: The warped space opened its jaws, and beyond the gap, where only darkness rippled, beings that had remained hidden until now emerged.
hunks.sol: Warped space opened its jaws. Beyond the gap, where only darkness rippled, beings that had remained hidden until now emerged.

hunks.baseline: Sharp spears and blades. Armor covering them from head to toe without a gap.
hunks.sol: Sharp spears and blades. Armor covering every inch of their bodies.

hunks.baseline: They numbered in the thousands and resembled one another like twins born of the same womb, and Jin Taekyung recalled the first day he’d returned to this world.
hunks.sol: There were hundreds of them—thousands—and they resembled one another like twins born of the same womb. Jin Taekyung recalled the first day he’d returned to this world.

hunks.baseline: Guardians born of Dragons and existing only for Dragons.
hunks.sol: Guardians born of Dragons and existing only to serve Dragons.

hunks.baseline: But that wasn’t all that made Jin Taekyung go rigid.
hunks.sol: But they weren’t the only thing that made Jin Taekyung freeze.

hunks.baseline: At the familiar face among the Dragon-tooth soldiers, a low groan slipped from his lips.
hunks.sol: A familiar face appeared among the Dragon-tooth soldiers, and a low groan escaped his lips.
